modifications: Converted from TEI XML to plain text paragraphs with emphasis, with the long s printed as s. Each exposition opens with the words of the text it expounds as Hutcheson printed them, such as Verse 1. In the beginning was the Word, and the paragraphs after a quotation stay with its verse. On Job and John each exposition the transcription divides off is one section, keyed by the verse label printed at its head, such as Verse 1. or Vers. 6. On the Minor Prophets each quotation's label opens a section; a label misprinted between two that follow on is read as the number between them, and a label that cannot stand in its chapter's order continues the section before it. A verse named in an argument or in the exposition, such as ver. 4., is never read. Two labels in Job the print gets wrong are read as the verse their text quotes: Job 21:21, printed 22, and Job 33:2, printed 3. A section runs from its own verse to the verse before the next section or the end of its chapter. A book's or chapter's argument opens its first section. Every gap the transcribers could not key is kept as the mark they gave it, such as • for an illegible letter and 〈◊〉 for an illegible word. Line-end hyphens are closed up. Left out: the title pages, the half-titles, the dedications, the epistles to the reader, the licensers' epistles and imprimaturs, the errata, the booksellers' lists, and the chapter headings such as CHAP. I.
